text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Daniel arap Moi announces that voter registration for this year's general election will begin this month.
- A Kenyan delegation is in Ethiopia to negotiate compensation for Kenyan families killed in clashes along the common border last week.
- Visiting Japanese delegation on economic co-operation expresses concern over the deteriorating security situation in Kenya, saying it could discourage foreign investment.
- Kenyan judges say they need to be better paid if they are to work effectively and efficiently.
- President Moi says the government will on Friday release cheques for the National Youth Development Fund.
- Two women are washed away by a seasonally flooded river in western Kenya.

- Brigadier John Odongo, who has lived in self-imposed exile in Ghana since being accused by the government of setting up a clandestine guerrilla group in 1995, is back in Kenya for his mother's burial.

- Opposition leaders and the National Council of Non- Govenmental Organisations are heading for collision at the start of the National Constitution Convention on Friday as both sides are pushing a different agenda.
- Nairobi's provincial administration bans the manufacture, sale and carrying of offensive weapons in the city.
- President Moi rebukes members of the ruling KANU party for what he calls continued laxity in the countdown to the general election.
- Apprehension within shipping circles is growing over the future of the Kenya Ports Authority following the expiry of the two-year contract of its chairman, Robert Brenneisen.
- Opposition leaders Kenneth Matiba and Raila Odinga reaffirm their commitment to working together.
